transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's capital-request meeting. We have the high school's proposal for a digital music production lab on the table — 10 laptops, a commercial cloud music platform, $8,000 from the general fund, and installation targeted for September 1, 2026. Before I make my final approval decision, I'd like to hear from each of you on any relevant findings. Could the requesting teacher, our instructional technology specialist, and the business-office manager please report what you've found regarding this proposal?

transcript.text: Dr. Monroe, I have an important finding to report. I completed a classroom trial this week with the enrolled section, and it showed that all 12 students need simultaneous stations — each student requires one laptop and one USB microphone. I recorded the results in my classroom planning log, but the log was not attached to the capital request. This means the proposal's request for 10 laptops may be insufficient, and USB microphones are not currently included in the draft.

transcript.text: Dr. Monroe, I've completed my network and privacy review for this proposal. The commercial cloud music platform cannot be used with student accounts — it fails our privacy and security requirements. However, the district-managed SoundLab EDU platform is approved and can support this course. It requires managed student accounts plus a security configuration record. I closed the technology review ticket this week, but it has not yet been linked to the purchasing request. The proposal should be revised to substitute SoundLab EDU for the commercial cloud platform.

transcript.text: Dr. Monroe, I have an important funding finding to report. I confirmed this week that the Arts Innovation Grant will fund this project, but only up to exactly $6,800 — not the $8,000 currently requested from the general fund. Additionally, the grant requires that the purchase order be issued by August 20, 2026, and under the grant's purchasing sequence, procurement and setup must follow the purchase order, making September 15, 2026 the earliest feasible installation date — not September 1 as proposed. I received the grant award notice this week and filed it in the business-office grant folder, but this funding information has not yet been added to the proposal. The proposal should be revised to reflect the $6,800 grant cap, the August 20 purchase order deadline, and the September 15, 2026 installation date.
